description: Overtime pay and total gross pay from your hourly rate, the hours you worked and when overtime starts. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

currency.description: ISO 4217 code such as USD, EUR, GBP, JPY. Decides the rounding: cents for most, whole units for JPY and KRW, thousandths for KWD. Defaults to USD.

dailyThreshold.description: Per-day list only: hours in a day after which that day's hours are overtime, e.g. 8 for California. Weekly overtime is then counted on the remaining regular hours only, so no hour is paid as overtime twice.

doubleTimeAfter.description: Optional second tier: hours after which pay is doubleTimeMultiplier × the rate instead. Counted in the same period as the threshold for a single number, and per day for a per-day list (California: 12). Must be above the threshold it follows.

doubleTimeMultiplier.description: Multiplier for hours past doubleTimeAfter. Defaults to 2; must not be lower than multiplier.

hourlyRate.description: Normal (straight-time) pay per hour, in major units of the currency: 25 for $25.00, 1500 for ¥1500.

hoursWorked.description: Hours worked, as decimal hours (7.5 = 7 h 30 min). Either one number for the whole period (see `period`), or a list of up to 7 numbers, one per day of a single week, e.g. [10, 10, 10, 10, 0, 0, 0]; the list is what makes `dailyThreshold` count. Overtime under the US FLSA is per workweek, so send one week at a time.

multiplier.description: Overtime pay multiplier: 1.5 (default) is time and a half, 2 is double time, 1.25 is a 25% premium.

period.description: What a single hoursWorked number and the threshold cover: "week" (default) or "day". Ignored for a per-day list, which is always one week.

threshold.description: Hours in the period after which overtime starts. Defaults to 40, the US federal weekly rule. With a per-day list this is the weekly threshold. 0 makes every hour overtime.
